rationales: Electronic configuration was not the basis of Mendeleev’s table.
Atomic number was used as the basis of the modern periodic table.
Mendeleev arranged elements mainly in order of increasing atomic mass.
Completion of subshells was not the basis of Mendeleev’s table.
Mass number is not the basis of the long-form periodic table.
Mendeleev’s postulate is not the defining basis of the long-form table.
The long-form periodic table is arranged by increasing atomic number.
Atomic mass was the basis of Mendeleev’s table, not the long-form table.
A triple covalent bond does not involve only three electrons.
Four electrons make two shared pairs, as in a double bond.
A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Eight electrons are not shared in a triple bond.
A single line represents a single covalent bond.
Two parallel lines represent a double covalent bond.
Three parallel lines represent a triple covalent bond.
An arrow represents a coordinate covalent bond, not a double bond.
Rubber is generally classified as an amorphous solid.
Plastic is generally classified as an amorphous solid.
Glucose forms crystals, so it is not amorphous.
Glass is an amorphous solid.
Chromium’s oxidation number is not +7 in this compound.
The total oxidation number of both chromium atoms is not +14.
Each chromium atom has oxidation number +6 in K₂Cr₂O₇.
Chromium’s oxidation number is not +2 in this compound.
Carbon is not the lustrous non-metal intended here.
Phosphorus is generally not lustrous.
Sulphur is generally not lustrous.
Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
Goldstein discovered canal rays, not the proton itself.
J. J. Thomson discovered the electron.
Bohr did not discover the proton.
Rutherford is credited with discovering the proton.
H₂ contains two atoms and is diatomic.
O₂ contains two atoms and is diatomic.
Cl₂ contains two atoms and is diatomic.
CO₂ contains three atoms and is triatomic.
The fourth and fifth periods are longer than the short periods.
The second and third periods are called short periods.
The fourth and fifth periods are called long periods.
The sixth period is very long, not the fourth and fifth.
Sugar solution does not form ions in water and is a non-electrolyte.
Sulphuric acid solution forms ions and conducts electricity.
Lime solution contains ions and conducts electricity.
Sodium chloride solution forms ions and conducts electricity.
HCl has a single bond, while O₂ has a double bond.
N₂ has a triple bond, while O₂ has a double bond.
C₂H₄ and O₂ each contain a double covalent bond.
C₂H₂ has a triple bond, while O₂ has a double bond.
Covalent bonding typically involves sharing electrons between non-metals.
An electropositive and an electronegative element typically form an ionic bond by electron transfer.
Polar covalent bonding involves unequal sharing, usually between non-metals.
Coordinate covalent bonding involves a shared pair donated by one atom.
Air is generally a homogeneous mixture of gases.
Rock is heterogeneous because its composition and components vary.
Gasoline is generally treated as a homogeneous mixture.
Iodine is an element, not a mixture.
J. J. Thomson proposed the plum pudding model of the atom.
Goldstein is known for discovering canal rays, not proposing the model.
Bohr proposed a model with electrons in quantized energy levels.
Chadwick discovered the neutron.
